prerequisites: Having partially met the learning objectives of the following second-year courses: Programming Technologies and Paradigms, Human-Computer Interaction, and Databases.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to design, develop, select and evaluate applications, ensuring their reliability, security and quality, in accordance with ethical principles and current legislation and regulations.
Ability to plan, conceive, deploy and manage IT projects, services and systems in all areas, leading their implementation and continuous improvement and assessing their economic and social impact.
Ability to understand the importance of negotiation, effective work habits, leadership and communication skills in all software development environments.
Knowledge and application of software engineering principles, methodologies and life cycles.
Analyze and elaborate the different models that comprise the functional specification of a software system based on given requirements.
Prepare the technical design of a software system according to a specification.
Design and execute tests on the components of a software system.
Review and evaluate the specification and design of a software system.
Elaborate the development and implementation plan of an application.
Negotiate with the client the requirements and implementation deadlines of an application.
Make technical presentations of the different products elaborated during the development of a software system.
Participate in a team for the preparation of the specification and design of a software system.
Understand the specific problems of software projects in relation to other types of engineering projects.
Apply a methodology for defining a software system.
Know different approaches and methodologies for software development.
Know the main national and international standards for software development.

syllabus_topics: General problems and characteristics of software
Main life cycle processes and techniques:

assessment_methods.method: Practical work (team and individual) during the course, considering student work (individual, team, and oral presentation) and delivered results.

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, a minimum of 4 points out of 10 is required in both the theory and practical parts. If this requirement is met, the final grade is the weighted average of theory and practice (50% each). If not met, the final grade will be the weighted average with a maximum of 4 points. For extraordinary calls, theory and practical grades from the ordinary call will be used if at least 5 points out of 10 were obtained; otherwise, these parts will be re-evaluated. A minimum of 5 points out of 10 is required in each part. If this is met, the final grade is the weighted average (50% each); otherwise, the grade will be the weighted average with a maximum of 4 points. For students with differentiated evaluation, both theory and practice will be assessed through specific tests, requiring a minimum of 5 points out of 10 in each part for a 50/50 weighted average, otherwise a maximum of 4 points.
